FleetDNA data density for single-unit short-haul vehicles Figure 4 shows data density for refuse trucks. FleetDNA contains no data for refuse trucks that travel on rural roads (shaded gray). Additionally, few refuse trucks from FleetDNA are observed driving on urban freeways on the weekend, so this category will be excluded from further visualization (shaded gray). For refuse trucks traveling on other urban roads on the weekend, results should be interpreted with caution, as there were only six vehicles for a few hours in many categories (shaded yellow). Refuse truck data on urban freeways on weekdays are also not as robust in vehicle or hour data and should perhaps be examined with caution (shaded yellow). On other urban roads on weekdays, there are over 30 vehicles, which statistically constitutes a good sample size and over 400 hours of data; the data in this group are relatively robust (no shading). 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 4. FleetDNA data density for refuse trucks Figure 5 illustrates data density for transit buses in FleetDNA. Although ordinarily we apply a threshold in the upper 20s of vehicle counts to determine good data coverage, the transit data were observed to contain three fleets from across the country despite having only 16 vehicles. On weekends, not all buses drove on urban other roads despite reasonable time coverage, so results should be interpreted with some care (shaded yellow). Due to the extremely low time recorded per hour for urban freeways on weekends, we will exclude them from further analysis (shaded gray). On weekdays, urban freeways have good representation of vehicles but not enough hours of data to be considered a sample with solid coverage (shaded yellow). We allow transit data on other urban roads on weekdays to be considered robust because of the hundreds of recorded hours and makeup of three distinct fleets, despite a smaller vehicle count than other source types. Categories with no recorded data have been shaded gray. 13 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 5. FleetDNA data density for transit buses Figure 6 illustrates the data density for the four school buses, which are only observed driving on weekdays on urban other roads (categories with no data have been shaded gray). We have decided to analyze the school bus urban other road data in the following sections. Despite the small sample size, we believe these data better represent school bus activity compared to using the aggregate medium-duty commercial data used in the MOVES3 default. We have categorized the data in yellow because the data should be analyzed with caution. 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
